skill.name: ui-ux-designer
skill.description: Create accessible interface designs, wireframes, user flows, design systems, and implementation guidance for modern digital products.
skill.summary: Guides accessible UI/UX design, research planning, design systems, and developer handoff.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to turn user needs into consistent, accessible interfaces. This skill guides research, flows, design systems, tokens, and handoff.
actual_capabilities: Plan user research, interviews, usability tests, and journey maps.
Create wireframes, user flows, information architecture, and interaction patterns.
Design accessible interfaces using WCAG guidance and inclusive design practices.
Define design tokens, component libraries, variants, and governance workflows.
Prepare developer handoff guidance for responsive web, mobile, and desktop products.
Recommend validation methods, success metrics, and iteration plans.
limitations: It does not create finished visual files inside Figma or other design tools by itself.
It relies on provided product context, audience details, and constraints for precise recommendations.
It cannot replace direct usability testing with real users.
It provides design guidance, not legal certification for accessibility compliance.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Redesign
use_cases.description: Map user goals, research questions, flows, and accessibility requirements before redesign work begins.

use_cases.title: Build a Design System
use_cases.description: Define tokens, components, documentation, governance, and handoff rules for a scalable interface system.

use_cases.title: Improve Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: Translate design decisions into responsive behavior, states, accessibility notes, and developer-ready specifications.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this screen for usability, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and clarity. Provide prioritized fixes with short reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Create a User Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a user flow for [task] used by [audience]. Include entry points, key screens, decisions, errors, and success states.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Component Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a component plan for [product area]. Include variants, states, accessibility requirements, tokens, and documentation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this end-to-end experience for user goals, conversion, accessibility, cross-platform consistency, and validation metrics.

output_examples.input: Review a SaaS dashboard for usability and accessibility.
output: Prioritized findings covering navigation, scanability, contrast, keyboard access, and empty states.
Recommended layout changes for clearer hierarchy and faster repeated use.
Validation plan with task-based testing and measurable success criteria.

output_examples.input: Create a design system plan for a multi-brand product suite.
output: Token architecture for color, type, spacing, elevation, and themes.
Component inventory with variants, states, documentation needs, and governance roles.
Adoption plan for design reviews, release notes, and developer handoff.

output_examples.input: Improve onboarding for a mobile app.
output: Revised onboarding flow with clearer decision points and reduced cognitive load.
Accessibility notes for touch targets, labels, focus order, and readable language.
Experiment plan comparing completion, activation, and early retention.

best_practices: Provide audience, platform, product goals, constraints, and any existing design system rules.
Ask for research assumptions, accessibility checks, and validation metrics in the same request.
Use the output as a design brief, then test important flows with real users.
anti_patterns: Do not request only visual polish when the workflow, content, or user goal is unclear.
Do not skip accessibility requirements until the end of the design process.
Do not treat generated recommendations as final without stakeholder and user validation.

faq.question: Can this skill create wireframes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe wireframes, layouts, screen structure, and interaction behavior for designers or developers to implement.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review contrast, focus behavior, keyboard access, semantics, labels, and inclusive design considerations.

faq.question: Can it build a full design system?
faq.answer: It can plan tokens, components, variants, documentation, governance, and handoff. It does not publish assets to a design tool.

faq.question: Is it useful for developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can translate design intent into responsive rules, states, accessibility notes, and implementation guidance.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide users, goals, platform, constraints, existing screens, brand rules, accessibility targets, and business metrics.

faq.question: Can it replace user research?
faq.answer: No. It can plan research and interpret findings, but real user feedback is still needed for high-confidence decisions.
